results.title: Batch of 2025-26 Results
results.body:
Lawrence High School ICSE congratulates the Batch of 2025-26 on a 100% result.

Distinctions (85% and above): 85 students.
58 students scored above 90, 27 students scored 85–89%, 15 students scored 80–84%, and 29 students scored 60–80%.

events.title: Independence Day
events.text: The Independence Day celebration for Grade 1 was filled with joy, enthusiasm, and patriotic spirit.
events.body:
The Independence Day celebration for Grade 1 was filled with joy, enthusiasm, and patriotic spirit. The children came dressed in colourful costumes representing various national figures. They were taken to the ground to participate in the flag-hoisting ceremony and proudly joined in the celebrations.

The children showed great enthusiasm during the fancy-dress activity and spoke confidently about the characters they represented. Later, they were given outlines of national symbols and asked to decorate them using tri-coloured paper. Working in groups, the children thoroughly enjoyed the creative activity and participated with great excitement.

Overall, it was a memorable and meaningful celebration that helped the children learn about our nation while having fun.

photos.alt: Students and teachers gathered for the Independence Day assembly
Flag hoisting on Independence Day at Lawrence High School
Grade 1 children in costume for the Independence Day celebration

events.title: Investiture Ceremony
events.text: Student leaders of 2026–27 received their badges, sashes and house flags.
events.body:
The Investiture Ceremony for 2026–27 welcomed the new student council to office. Head Girl, house captains and sports leaders stood on stage with their sashes and flags, ready to serve the school.

Teachers presented the house flags, and the student leaders accepted them as a promise to lead with integrity and respect. The ceremony reminded everyone that leadership is not about being in charge. It is about inspiring others and working together for a better tomorrow.

It was a proud morning for the school, as the new team stepped forward to guide their houses and set an example for every Lawrence student.

photos.alt: Head Girl and sports leaders with the school flags at the Investiture Ceremony
A teacher presenting the house flag to a student captain
The student council and teachers on stage at the Investiture Ceremony

events.title: Dad and Me
events.text: Fathers joined their children in class for a morning of drawing, building and photographs.
events.body:
Dad and Me brought fathers into the classroom to spend the morning with their children. They sat together at the tables, drawing, writing and building with colourful blocks.

A photo frame decorated with “Best Dad” and “My Hero” became a favourite stop. Fathers and children posed together, proud and happy to be side by side.

It was a warm morning that let every child show their father what school feels like, and let every father see the joy of learning up close.

photos.alt: Fathers drawing and building with their children during Dad and Me
A father and child posing in the Best Dad photo frame
A father holding his child in the My Hero photo frame

events.title: Mom and Me
events.text: Mothers joined their children to paint pots and celebrate together.
events.body:
Mom and Me brought mothers into school to create something with their children. Together they painted clay pots, adding bright colours and patterns at the table.

Some children came dressed for Krishna Janmashtami, with crowns, beads and festive clothes. Mothers sat beside them, guiding little hands and sharing the work.

The morning ended in front of a Happy Janmashtami backdrop, with mothers and children greeting the celebration side by side.

photos.alt: A mother and child painting a clay pot together
A child dressed as Krishna decorating a pot with his mother
A mother and child in front of the Happy Janmashtami display

events.title: Best Out of Waste
events.text: Students turned paper, sticks and everyday bits into new creations.
events.body:
Best Out of Waste invited students to make something new from materials that might otherwise be thrown away. Classrooms filled with paper, ice-cream sticks, glue and colour as everyone set to work.

Some folded bright paper fans and hanging decorations. Others built pictures, including a fish made from small reused pieces, and held them up with pride.

The competition showed how a little imagination can turn ordinary scraps into something worth keeping.

photos.alt: A student showing a paper fan made for Best Out of Waste
A student holding a fish picture made from reused materials
Students crafting with sticks, paper and glue during Best Out of Waste

events.title: Drawing and Colouring
events.text: Students filled their pages with boats, rainbows, houses and colour.
events.body:
Drawing and Colouring gave every class a quiet hour with pencils, crayons and paper. Students bent over their desks, adding lines and colour to pictures of their own.

When the work was done, they held their drawings up to share. Boats on the water, rainbows over little houses, bright landscapes and colourful kites all found a place on the page.

It was a simple afternoon that let imagination lead, one colour at a time.

photos.alt: Students drawing at their desks during Drawing and Colouring
Three students showing their coloured drawings of a boat, a rainbow and a house
Students showing their coloured kite pictures from the colouring competition

events.title: Robotic Fest
events.text: Students demonstrated robots and explained their projects to visitors.
events.body:
Robotic Fest turned the hall into a showcase of student ideas. Tables were lined with models, laptops and small robots, and every team was ready to explain how their project worked.

Visitors watched a robot car run across the floor and stopped at displays such as health-care robots. Students talked through their designs, from the parts on the table to the posters behind them.

It was a lively morning of building, testing and sharing, and a chance for the school to see what young inventors can do.

photos.alt: Students demonstrating a small robot car at Robotic Fest
Students presenting a health-care robot project
Students explaining their model to visitors at Robotic Fest

events.title: Awareness Week
events.text: Students learned to care for the earth with cloth bags, seeds and planting.
events.body:
Awareness Week turned everyday choices into lessons. Students held up a globe, a cloth bag and a plastic bag, and talked about why a reusable bag is kinder to the earth.

In class they pressed seeds onto cardboard rolls and filled pots with soil. Hands got messy, and everyone leaned in to help.

By the end of the week, the children had planted something of their own and taken home a simple idea: small habits can look after the planet.

photos.alt: Students comparing a cloth bag and a plastic bag beside a globe
Students pressing seeds onto a cardboard roll
Students planting seeds in a pot during Awareness Week

events.title: Fancy Dress
events.text: Students dressed as fruits, heroes, a firefighter and a rocket for the competition.
events.body:
The Fancy Dress Competition filled the classroom with colour and character. Children arrived as fruits, princesses, soldiers, an astronaut and even a dinosaur, and lined up to show who they had become.

One student came as a firefighter, ready to save lives, with a bright engine painted beside him. Another stepped in as an Indian rocket, complete with the tricolour and boosters.

Each child spoke for their character, and the morning became a parade of imagination.

photos.alt: Students in costume for the Fancy Dress Competition
A student dressed as a firefighter at the Fancy Dress Competition
A student wearing an Indian rocket costume at the Fancy Dress Competition

events.title: Field Trip
events.text: Students stepped outside school to meet the people who keep the city clean and to explore a garden.
events.body:
The field trip took the children beyond the classroom. They met workers from Clean Bengaluru, who keep the city tidy, and received a small card as a reminder of the work that happens every day.

Out in the open, the class crouched together to look closely at the ground, curious about what they could find. Later they gathered under a bright arch of painted pots in a green garden.

It was a day of looking, listening and learning in the world outside school.

photos.alt: A student receiving a card from a Clean Bengaluru worker
Students looking closely at the ground during the field trip
Students posing under a painted pot arch in the garden

events.title: Krishna Janmashtami
events.text: Grades 1 students celebrated Janmashtami with great devotion and joy on 4th September during the General Assembly.
events.body:
Grades 1 students celebrated Janmashtami with great devotion and joy on 4th September during the General Assembly. The sandpit area was beautifully decorated with colorful matkas, flutes, and chart papers, creating a festive atmosphere.

The celebration began with the school prayer, followed by students presenting dance, music, shlokas, thought for the day, and word for the day. Many children came dressed as Krishna, Radha, and Gopikas, adding charm to the celebration.

Students also presented a beautiful Radha-Krishna dance at their level, showcasing their enthusiasm and devotion. The celebration helped students learn about the importance of the festival and feel proud of our rich culture.

photos.alt: A teacher and student in costume holding a decorated matka for Janmashtami
Students performing a dance for Krishna Janmashtami
Students dressed as Krishna and Radha for Janmashtami

events.title: Making Learning Visible
events.text: Parents sat with their children and watched letter games unfold at the table.
events.body:
Making Learning Visible opened the classroom so families could see how children learn. Parents sat beside their little ones as letters, pictures and matching games covered the tables.

One child paired letter shapes on a black board. Another matched letters with objects in the house, picking cards from a plate while a teacher guided the next step. A teacher also helped a child use a dropper, watching coloured water travel into cotton.

It was a close look at everyday learning: small hands, careful choices, and families watching the work happen.

photos.alt: A child matching letter pairs while parents watch
A child matching letters with objects as a teacher and parent look on
A teacher helping a child use a dropper with coloured water and cotton

events.title: Role Play
events.text: Students stepped into character as a chef, an astronaut and a teacher.
events.body:
Role Play let students try on someone else’s day. In a chef’s hat and apron, one child held a bowl and spoke as if the classroom were a kitchen.

Another arrived in a silver space suit, ready for a mission. A third came as a teacher, with a bag, a book and a shawl, standing ready to take the class.

By becoming the character, the children practised words, confidence and a little imagination.

photos.alt: A student dressed as a chef for the Role Play competition
A student in an astronaut costume for the Role Play competition
A student dressed as a teacher for the Role Play competition

events.title: Teachers' Day
events.text: Students thank the teachers who guide them from the first classroom to the laboratory.
events.body:
Teachers' Day is the school's chance to thank the people who guide every child. The thanks belong in many rooms, not only on a stage.

In the early years, a teacher sits at the table and turns play into learning. With older children, a music lesson becomes a shared discovery. In the laboratory, a teacher stands with students as they test an idea for themselves.

The day is a reminder of that everyday work, and of the teachers who help Lawrence students grow.

photos.alt: A kindergarten teacher exploring with students at Lawrence High School
A teacher making music with children in class
A teacher guiding high school students in the science laboratory

achievements.title: Aditi Dash Selected Among Top 100 Science Talents in India
achievements.body:
Aditi Dash of Grade VI has secured 2nd Rank and has been selected among the Top 100 Science Talents in India through the National Science Promotion Orient Test (SPOT) 2025–2026, conducted by the Vikram Sarabhai Science Foundation (VSSF), Kochi.

She has been invited to attend the VSSF Internship Programme in Bengaluru from 17th to 19th July 2026 where she will have the unique opportunity to interact with scientists from ISRO, gain first-hand exposure to scientific concepts and live experiments, and receive her SPOT 100 Badge, Medal, and Certificate of Merit.
